stem.astronomy.journey_m_first_look_hint: Visit the Observatory and look around the sky for your place and time.
stem.astronomy.journey_m_name_it_hint: In the Observatory, select any star, planet or the Moon to learn what it is.
stem.astronomy.journey_m_wanderer_hint: Select a planet or the Moon in the Observatory. The word planet comes from a Greek word for wanderer, because planets drift against the stars.
stem.astronomy.journey_m_five_lights_hin: Identify five different objects in the Observatory. Selecting the same one twice counts once.
stem.astronomy.journey_m_deep_sky_hint: Select a deep-sky object, such as a nebula, star cluster or galaxy, in the Observatory.
stem.astronomy.journey_m_plan_night_hint: Select an object in the Observatory and add it to tonight’s list. The Print section turns the list into a timetable.
stem.astronomy.journey_m_new_place_hint: Change the Observatory place. The same night looks different from Maine, Chile or Norway.
stem.astronomy.journey_m_time_traveler_h: Move the deep-time control in the Observatory to watch the stars drift over thousands of years.
stem.astronomy.journey_m_pattern_finder_: Save three constellations to your observing list from the Constellations section.
stem.astronomy.journey_m_sky_traditions_: Read about two different traditions in Sky Traditions.
stem.astronomy.journey_m_simulators_hint: Open three of the simulators: Moon, Eclipses, Exoplanets, Seasons or Star diagram.
stem.astronomy.journey_m_daily_question_: Answer the sky question at the top of the Tonight page.
stem.astronomy.journey_m_quiz_ace_hint: Score at least 80% on the quiz.
stem.astronomy.dq_moon_direction_q: At {time} tonight the Moon is {pct}% lit. Is it waxing (growing) or waning (shrinking)?
stem.astronomy.dq_moon_waxing_e: It is waxing. About {age} days after new Moon, the lit part is still growing night by night toward full Moon.
stem.astronomy.dq_moon_waning_e: It is waning. About {age} days after new Moon is past the halfway point of the cycle, so the lit part is shrinking toward the next new Moon.
stem.astronomy.dq_higher_q: At {time} tonight from {place}, which is higher above the horizon: {a} or {b}?
stem.astronomy.dq_higher_e: {high} is about {highAlt}° above the horizon and {low} is about {lowAlt}°.
stem.astronomy.dq_planet_q: Which of these planets is above the horizon at {time} tonight from {place}?
stem.astronomy.dq_planet_e: {planet} is about {alt}° above the horizon. The other two are below it at that time, so they are hidden from view.
stem.astronomy.dq_dark_q: About how many hours will the sky be fully dark (the Sun more than 18° below the horizon) at {place} on the night that begins on {date}?
stem.astronomy.dq_dark_zero_e: None. At this place and date the Sun never sinks more than 18° below the horizon, so the sky never gets fully dark.
stem.astronomy.dq_dark_e: About {hours}. The Sun’s calculated height is checked every 10 minutes from noon to noon, and the sky counts as fully dark when the Sun is more than 18° below the horizon.
stem.astronomy.dq_star_q: At {time} tonight from {place}, which direction do you face to find the star {star}?
stem.astronomy.dq_star_e: {star} is about {alt}° above the horizon, at compass bearing {az}° ({dir}).
stem.astronomy.dq_phase_q: The Moon is {pct}% lit tonight and about {age} days past new Moon. What phase is it in?
stem.astronomy.dq_phase_e: {phase}. {pct}% of the Moon’s face is lit about {age} days into its cycle.
stem.astronomy.journey_daily_scope: Calculated for {place} at {time} on {date}, using the same sky model as the Observatory.
stem.astronomy.journey_intro: Missions are optional, never expire and can be done in any order. They point you at interesting things to try.
stem.astronomy.journey_all_done: Every mission is complete. Keep exploring: the sky is different every night.
stem.astronomy.journey_days: Days exploring: {n}. There is no streak to lose; come back whenever you like.
stem.astronomy.journey_days_run: Days in a row right now: {n}.
stem.astronomy.journey_daily_unavailable: Today’s question could not be calculated for this place. Choose another place in the Observatory.
stem.astronomy.journey_daily_tomorrow: A new question arrives tomorrow. Changing the place in the Observatory gives that place its own question.
stem.astronomy.quiz_feedback_high: Excellent work. You know this sky well.
stem.astronomy.quiz_feedback_mid: A solid start. Read the explanations below, then try again whenever you like.
stem.astronomy.quiz_feedback_low: Every astronomer starts here. The explanations below show how each answer works, and you can retake the quiz at any time.
stem.astronomy.quiz_practice: Practice mode: show feedback after each answer
stem.astronomy.quiz_practice_help: Each answer locks once you choose it and the explanation appears right away. Your first answers still count toward your score.
stem.astronomy.quiz_open_note: Question {n} needs an answer before you can submit. {count} questions are still open.
